Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: RISA publishes news and policy updates on its website. National Data Sharing Policy is publicly available. IAPP analysis and Cenfri analysis published about Rwanda's policy. RISA participates in public events (Africa HealthTech Summit 2025). The DSP will include monitoring, auditing, and reporting functions.

revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched and confirmed genuine: RISA's news page confirms Cabinet approved the National Data Sharing Policy on 26 May 2025, and the IAPP analysis (18 June 2025) corroborates this and describes the policy's scope. However, neither source demonstrates recurring 'Annual Reports' on data exchange operations, which is what a code of 3 requires under the scale. A check of RISA's own public 'Reports' page (risa.gov.rw/publications/reports) turned up only an ITU Cybersecurity Index report and an African Smart City Index report — nothing on the data exchange/data sharing platform itself. The Data Sharing Platform portal (data.gov.rw) exposes no public reporting content. The policy document states the future Data Sharing Platform 'will include' monitoring, auditing and reporting functions, i.e. this is a planned capability, not evidence of current annual reporting. On the evidence available, disclosure consists of one-off policy publication and news coverage rather than a recurring public reporting product, which better matches code 2 (Low = Limited Disclosure) than code 3 (Moderate = Annual Reports). This is a judgement call on a borderline case rather than a clear-cut error, so it is flagged for human review rather than asserted outright.
revised_comments: Rwanda's data exchange governance is disclosed through the National Data Sharing Policy, approved by Cabinet on 26 May 2025 under the leadership of the Ministry of ICT and Innovation (MINICT) and the Rwanda Information Society Authority (RISA). The policy document, which establishes the governance structures, Data Governance Unit, and the planned Data Sharing Platform, is publicly available, and its approval has been covered in professional analysis (IAPP, June 2025). Disclosure to date takes the form of the published policy and occasional news updates on RISA's website rather than a recurring public reporting product such as an annual report or public dashboard on data exchange operations.
